independent_numerical_and_reasoning_chec.name: larger inflow action endpoints at y=-0.1

exercise_reviews.label: Exercise P1.B1 — Medium: The upper boundary needs its own filter
exercise_reviews.mathematics_review: The compatible state interval [9.7,9.9] and disturbance interval yield [9.5+u,10.1+u]. Containment and actuator intersection give [-1,-0.1]; projection of 0.7 gives -0.1, correction 0.8 and attained successors 9.4 and 10.
exercise_reviews.depth_review: All requested quantities are derived from the uncertainty model, both endpoint inequalities are solved, the nearest-point choice is justified and both extreme substitutions are shown with units.

exercise_reviews.label: Exercise P1.B2 — Hard: A larger inflow can destroy recursive feasibility
exercise_reviews.mathematics_review: The new sufficient interval is [1.3-y,8.7-y]. Allowed x=0 and sensor error -0.1 give [1.4,8.8], disjoint from the actuator interval. The independent obstruction x=0,w=-1.2 requires u>=1.2, showing the genuine invariance failure.
exercise_reviews.depth_review: The changed combined uncertainty, each solved safety inequality, validity of the boundary measurement and distinction between sufficient-certificate failure and actual impossibility are explained.

exercise_reviews.label: Exercise P1.B3 — Hard: Write the quantifiers in the right order
exercise_reviews.mathematics_review: Every valid measurement is in [-0.1,10.1]; the quantified action depends on y and must handle every compatible x and w. The sufficient interval has ordered endpoints, lower endpoint <=1 and upper endpoint >=-1, proving nonempty actuator intersection. Boundary states demand incompatible constant-input inequalities.
exercise_reviews.depth_review: The hidden-state information set and complete quantifier order are explicit; the answer proves feedback feasibility as well as the constant-input contradiction and connects one-step preservation to repeated filtering.

exercise_reviews.label: Exercise P2.B1 — Medium: A noisier observation changes the first experiment
exercise_reviews.mathematics_review: The lower observed margin is 0.13; division by the positive Lipschitz constant gives radius 0.26 and domain intersection [0,0.46]. At 0.5 the lower margin is -0.02. Endpoint 0.46 has lower margin zero and is permitted only under the non-strict test.
exercise_reviews.depth_review: The answer derives the bound from measurement error, solves the absolute-value inequality, displays the pre-intersection interval and distinguishes uncertified from unsafe and strict from non-strict margins.

exercise_reviews.label: Exercise P2.B2 — Hard: Safety data need not certify optimal performance
exercise_reviews.mathematics_review: The second safety observation certifies [0,0.74], not a productivity ranking. Both p(a)=a and p(a)=-a are consistent with exactly the same safety information and select different certified-set optima. The true-safe-set optimization is correctly conditional on additional performance information.
exercise_reviews.depth_review: The missing performance function, direction and information are identified; the optimization problem is written and two concrete countermodels explain why safety readings cannot establish the proposed optimum.

exercise_reviews.label: Exercise P2.B3 — Hard: Handle a zero Lipschitz constant honestly
exercise_reviews.mathematics_review: A zero global Lipschitz constant forces equality of all function values. A lower margin 0.16 transfers to every point. If the only available information is a negative lower bound, the lower-bound test certifies nothing and does not prove negativity of the constant; division by zero is avoided.
exercise_reviews.depth_review: The defining inequality proves constancy, the positive case is propagated explicitly, and the stated information limitation in the negative case is respected rather than using an undefined radius.

exercise_reviews.label: Exercise P3.B1 — Medium: Feature units change the perturbation geometry
exercise_reviews.mathematics_review: Both normalized coordinates have bound 0.2 and remain in the stated affine-validity box. The exact lower gap is zero, attained at normalized (-0.2,0.2), corresponding to physical (-0.1,0.4). The physical coefficients (4,-1/2) give the identical worst change -0.6.
exercise_reviews.depth_review: Each unit conversion and coefficient substitution is shown; the bound is attained, so the strict certificate genuinely fails. The answer explains why changing the uncertainty set or metric without conversion changes the question.

exercise_reviews.label: Exercise P3.B2 — Hard: A calibration rank can exceed the data
exercise_reviews.mathematics_review: ceil(20*0.99)=20 exceeds 19 finite ranks. The augmented infinity convention gives a vacuous residual set. The exchangeable continuous no-tie counterexample has calibration-maximum coverage 19/20=0.95, so clipping cannot inherit a distribution-free 0.99 guarantee.
exercise_reviews.depth_review: The unavailable order statistic, conservative construction and interpretation are explicit. Uniform test-score rank gives a complete concrete reason for the failure of silent clipping, rather than a bare caution.

exercise_reviews.label: Exercise P3.B3 — Hard: Joint decisions need a joint guarantee
exercise_reviews.mathematics_review: Union failure is at most 0.4, hence success at least 0.6. Under mutual independence the product lower bound is 0.9^4=0.6561; equality requires all marginal success probabilities to be 0.9. Per-prediction failure <=0.025 yields joint failure <=0.1.
exercise_reviews.depth_review: Failure events, union and complement are defined; each probability substitution and the independence condition are shown. The final calibration qualification correctly prevents an allocated budget from being mistaken for an achieved guarantee.
